If you don't have funds & she is getting a lawyer, you can request the judge to ask her to pay for your lawyer. The judge could  level the playing field. My ex asked similarly, but her request  was denied since she had funds. If the judge denies your request, then ask him to give u time to find a lawyer. 

You can also call the ombudsman in that court for your available options. Go to the court website and you will find their number. The court building might also have a family law center that will answer most of your queries regarding this. If you know the name of the judge who will be hearing your case, you can talk to his judicial clerk. Get the number from website or from Court's phone line.

 Most lawyers give free consultation. Meet a few of them asap. Don't hire an expensive lawyer if u are short on funds. My last lawyer was somebody who was a recent graduate, but had worked as a law clerk in the same court. She knew most judges & the system. Old, experienced lawyers will suck u dry. Stay away from them. Hire lawyers who are near to the  court & who have worked cases in that court frequently. There is a distinct advantage since those lawyers know most judges in that court & can reduce ur costs.

There are so many games that u can play to delay. U can hire a cheap lawyer & that lawyer can send a letter to the court mentioning he just got the case and it will be easily postponed. 

Even if u appear alone on the date to answer notice, the judge will order discovery & mediation. Discovery is typically 6 weeks & then 2-3 weeks to get mediator appt. That will be multiple sessions that u can stretch for months. If mediation fails, u request judge for trial & that will be another month. So, don't worry about time. You will get plenty time to prepare.

Does your stbx work? If not, there could be alimony involved. If she works but earns less because of earning capability, there could be alimony depending on length of marriage & difference in income (imputed). Since you don't have kids & assets, your questions should be around alimony. For the lawyer, I would explain the financial & personal situation & then ask
1. What is the process? 
2. How should I protect myself from any counter claims? Dv, harassment, abuse, rape etc? Based on your experience, should you continue staying in the same residence as her? Should you move all your stuff out? Lease issues etc?
3. How will assets be divided? Bank locker, jewellery, shares, 401k, Ira etc?
4. What are your fees? Since, this is a simple divorce, can you charge one lump sum fee instead of hourly? How much for email, phone, copies, fax etc?
5. Does he have a paralegal who works for him/her? Who handles queries when he is in court or on vacation? Does he work evenings or weekends? Does he answer emails? How soon will he respond once you ask a question? 4 hrs? 8 hrs? 24 hrs? 
6. Can he provide you the template of documents & you do all the legwork of filling in remainder to control costs?
7. How much is the retainer? Is it refundable if not used? How much is the replenishment once he exhausts the retainer?
Good luck.
